To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) sunitinib can induce a partial response in patients with advanced GIST who have progressed after imatinib, and that (b) this partial response can be followed by transient resistance to sunitinibtreatment.
sunitinib may be reinitiated after a period of disease progression, even after other treatments, in patients with GIST.
the two patients with GIST who were resistant to sunitinibtreatment had a transient response when sunitinib was administered again after the other treatments failed.

the development of a new generation of drugs for the treatment of GISTs.
the development of a new method for the treatment of patients with GIST.
the study of the effect of the drug sunitinib on the proliferation of human cancer cell lines and the identification of potential biomarkers of response and resistance to the treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in patients with GISTs, the response to treatment is not permanent, and that the disease may recur after a period of remission.
sunitinib is a good drug for GIST and should be used for the treatment of GIST.
the majority of patients with GIST who develop resistance to imatinib or sunitinib can still benefit from other TKIs, such as regorafenib, dasatinib or nilotinib.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sunitinib can be rechallenged in patients who have previously responded and progressed.
we are not able to predict the duration of the response to a particular drug.
the transient sunitinib-resistance is a rare event, but that the possibility of re-sensitization should be kept in mind.

patients should not be denied the opportunity to try sunitinib again, even if they have previously progressed on it.
sunitinib can be effective in patients who progress after initial response to this drug.
